sources.license: Public domain (US Government work); OpenFEMA terms and conditions apply
sources.note: Flood insurance claims, redacted by FEMA to protect policyholders: location is given to the census block group and 0.1 degree, and some records carry no location at all. Counts are claims filed, not flooded homes; most flooded homes in Puerto Rico had no flood policy. Dollars are nominal. OpenFEMA terms: "This product uses the Federal Emergency Management Agency’s OpenFEMA API, but is not endorsed by FEMA. The Federal Government or FEMA cannot vouch for the data or analyses derived from these data after the data have been retrieved from the Agency's website(s)."

sources.name: NFIP Redacted Policies (v3)
sources.license: Public domain (US Government work); OpenFEMA terms and conditions apply
sources.note: Flood insurance policy terms, redacted by FEMA; updated about monthly, with a lag behind the system of record. Policies in force are derived here from effective, termination and cancellation dates; they are not an official FEMA count. Private flood insurance is not included. OpenFEMA terms: "This product uses the Federal Emergency Management Agency’s OpenFEMA API, but is not endorsed by FEMA. The Federal Government or FEMA cannot vouch for the data or analyses derived from these data after the data have been retrieved from the Agency's website(s)."

sources.name: Public Assistance Funded Projects Details (v2)
sources.license: Public domain (US Government work); OpenFEMA terms and conditions apply
sources.note: Obligated Public Assistance project worksheets. The municipio is where the applicant is, not always where the work is; projects FEMA lists as Statewide are kept island-wide. Projects still in pre-obligation processing are not in the data. Dollars are nominal. OpenFEMA terms: "This product uses the Federal Emergency Management Agency’s OpenFEMA API, but is not endorsed by FEMA. The Federal Government or FEMA cannot vouch for the data or analyses derived from these data after the data have been retrieved from the Agency's website(s)."

sources.name: Hazard Mitigation Assistance Subapplications (v2)
sources.license: Public domain (US Government work); OpenFEMA terms and conditions apply
sources.note: Hazard mitigation subapplications and subgrants in any status. FEMA says the data are subject to a small percentage of human error and that some fields were not provided. Dollars are nominal. OpenFEMA terms: "This product uses the Federal Emergency Management Agency’s OpenFEMA API, but is not endorsed by FEMA. The Federal Government or FEMA cannot vouch for the data or analyses derived from these data after the data have been retrieved from the Agency's website(s)."
